sourceKind: owner-export snapshot of already-public roadmap and backlog cards, owner-approved allowlist; source exports generated 2026-07-14 to 2026-11-13; not live

cards.title: Enable Account Portal to Fitness Handoff
cards.summary: Let people who begin in the Fawxzzy account portal continue straight into Fitness without a second sign-in step.

cards.title: Complete Self-Service Account Tools
cards.summary: Finish the self-service account lifecycle: recovering a forgotten sign-in, downloading your own data, and removing your account.

cards.title: Finish Account Site Setup for the Fitness App
cards.summary: Complete the shared account site that Fitness relies on for sign-in, sign-out, forgotten-sign-in recovery and returning people to the app, so the account side is finished before more Fitness work builds on it. Progress: the sign-in, sign-up and reset forms now list in plain language what is missing or wrong; this is live on the account site and has not been checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Add Active User and Product Usage Statistics
cards.summary: Track enough usage to understand activation and retention.

cards.title: Make Sign-In Outcomes Clear
cards.summary: Show a clear message whenever a sign-in attempt does not complete, instead of quietly returning to the sign-in form.

cards.title: Send Branded Account Messages for Fitness and Mazer
cards.summary: Account messages such as forgotten-sign-in recovery now come from one no-reply Fawxzzy sender with a per-app look (Fitness green, Mazer cyan). Checked live on 2026-11-10 with a throwaway account: the message arrived, its link opened the new sign-in form, a new sign-in was saved and sign-in worked. Not verified: sign-up and change-of-address messages, and other mail clients. The hourly send allowance was raised from 2 to 30 on 2026-11-11 (confirmed by reload); the delivery service's free tier allows 100 messages a day.

cards.title: Build Curated Workout Engine V1
cards.summary: Create a simple guided program generator so users can get a routine without designing one manually.

cards.title: Expand Curated Workout Engine Beyond V1
cards.summary: Improve the workout engine with smarter recommendations after the V1 generator exists.

cards.title: Add Achievements and Badges
cards.summary: Add lightweight achievements after core retention loops exist.

cards.title: Expand Achievements and Earned Notifications
cards.summary: Plan a richer deterministic achievements phase and once-only earned notifications after the current achievement review is accepted.

cards.title: Ship Curated Onboarding Intake And Generator Handoff
cards.summary: Turn the dormant curated onboarding flow into a real first-time guided setup lane that captures training goal, experience, equipment, schedule, preferences, and constraints, persists the intake per member, and hands the bounded payload to the curated engine contract without pretending generation exists when it does not.

cards.title: Expand Earned Install Promotion Moments
cards.summary: Expand the earned install prompt beyond the first shipped post-workout moment so install asks happen after real product value and only on supported device paths. This should remain a capability-aware promotion lane, not a return to install-first gating.

cards.title: Harden Atlas Contracts and CI Environment Verification
cards.summary: Keep Fitness contract exports and environment verification deterministic across local and hosted CI.

cards.title: Return a Proper Not-Found Status for Missing Pages
cards.summary: Pages for items that do not exist or are unavailable should respond with a real not-found status along with the friendly not-found screen.

cards.title: Ship Shareable Workout Recap Artifacts
cards.summary: Generate one deterministic workout recap artifact from completed session truth so users can review, share, or export a clean summary without building a social feed. The artifact should highlight workout summary, PR moments, and consistency signals when grounded in real data.

cards.title: Make Workout Start Atomic
cards.summary: Make starting a workout an all-or-nothing step so an interrupted start never leaves a partial session behind.

cards.title: Lock Down Database Access for Signed-Out Visitors
cards.summary: On 2026-11-10 signed-out visitors lost the ability to run 5 Fitness database functions and 5 internal tables became deny-by-default. The change was applied by approved hash and a rollback file is kept. Re-tested live afterward: sign-in, portal handoff, History and workout resume. Not verified: finishing a workout and reordering a routine were not clicked through.

cards.title: Add Calendar View
cards.summary: Give users a visual way to see training consistency over time.

cards.title: Add Workout Streaks
cards.summary: Add simple streak tracking to increase habit formation.

cards.title: Add Consistency Heatmap
cards.summary: Add GitHub-style workout consistency visualization.

cards.title: Add Weekly and Monthly Progress Summaries
cards.summary: Create periodic summaries that make progress feel real.

cards.title: Respect the Local Day Boundary in Workout Streaks
cards.summary: Count streak days in the user's local time zone so an evening workout is credited to the day it was logged.

cards.title: Add Optional Planned Workout Days
cards.summary: Distinguish optional workout days from required and rest days without weakening adherence, missed-day, or streak truth.

cards.title: Add Per-Exercise Exercise Timer System
cards.summary: Add a deterministic per-exercise timer system to session logging for exercises the user wants to time while they are actively performing them. The timer should be optional when an exercise is added, belong to the session exercise rather than the whole workout, appear during Current Session logging when enabled, and persist bounded timer outcomes for later analytics and history reuse.

cards.title: Add Exercise Timer Toggle When Adding an Exercise
cards.summary: Add a switch control in the add-exercise flow that enables or disables an exercise timer for that exercise in the current session. If enabled, the add flow should support a bounded timer configuration such as a target duration or timer mode. If disabled, the exercise should behave exactly like today with no timer UI added later in session logging.

cards.title: Show Live Per-Exercise Timer During Current Session Logging
cards.summary: When a timer-enabled exercise is open in Current Session, show the timer control in the logger surface for that exercise. The user should be able to start, pause, resume, reset, or dismiss the timer while performing the exercise without affecting the saved set truth. If a target duration exists, completion should surface a clear done-state cue for that exercise.

cards.title: Persist Exercise Timer Outcomes Into Session Analytics
cards.summary: Persist exercise-timer configuration and usable outcome data into session truth. At minimum, store whether the exercise used a timer, the configured timer target or mode when present, and enough completed timing data to support later summaries and comparisons. This must survive session completion and be available to history-family loaders without reconstructing timer behavior from fragile client-only state.

cards.title: Add Separate Recovery And Rest Recommendation Layer
cards.summary: Add a separate backend and product lane for recovery summaries, rest recommendations, and next-set prompts. This may use set timestamps, session history, and any later bounded timing truth, but it must remain a separate concern from the toggleable exercise timer feature. The app can later surface deterministic guidance such as likely rest windows or recovery patterns without redefining the user-facing exercise timer as a rest timer.

cards.title: Show Live Active User Presence on Today
cards.summary: Show a privacy-preserving aggregate active-user count on Today without exposing individual identities.

cards.title: Maintain the mobile-clean 2D shipping baseline: evidence rule and stale reference fixed
cards.summary: Keep the current Phaser maze readable, responsive, mechanically faithful, and regression-safe across supported desktop and mobile play. Merged to main, no player-visible change, so there is nothing to deploy-check. PR #474 (merged as 472b2eb2) fixed a stale demo-build reference and recorded the visual-baseline archival note so production claims stay tied to exact reviewed source. The card is an ongoing baseline; It stays active, not review: it is an ongoing baseline and the export tests need one active card as a lifecycle fixture.

cards.title: Adopt the shared account consumer contract
cards.summary: Use the canonical public-client authorization flow and shared account routes, keeping sensitive values out of the client and avoiding competing account screens.

cards.title: Harden sign-in: shared portal, refresh handling and retired-target rejection
cards.summary: Mazer replaced its own sign-in UI with the shared account portal (PR #350), restored the signed-out boot gate (PR #361), rejected retired provider targets (PR #364), fixed refresh and transient-failure handling (PR #370) and paused the menu AI until account access resolves (PR #369). Merged to main; live end-to-end acceptance is tracked separately.

cards.title: Finish the atomic sign-up username flow (blocked on provider)
cards.summary: Sign-up should claim the chosen username in the same step as account creation. The server-side contract merged (PR #280), but the client consumer in PR #281 is still open, conflicts with main and must not ship until the matching provider-side hook is confirmed live and proven. It has been open since 2026-08-25.

cards.title: Prove installed-app sign-in and progress end to end
cards.summary: Code fixes for retired-target rejection, AI progression hydration, menu-AI pause, session refresh and callback-error visibility are merged (PR #364, #367, #368, #369, #370). No end-to-end acceptance run exists yet: installed-app proof, natural session refresh, account recovery, cross-user isolation, authenticated progress hydration and whether the account handoff keeps an installed app standalone. It needs a real phone and a throwaway test account.

cards.title: Harden progress reset across devices with a reset epoch
cards.summary: Reset progress works server-first for one device, but a second device holding higher local progress would show the old level after a merge. The complete fix adds a reset counter on the server and makes both merge paths discard local data when it advances, which needs an approved database change. It has been held since 2026-11-06; version one may accept the residual risk. The owner delegated judgement calls on 2026-11-10 but a database change still needs explicit approval.

cards.title: Persist settings per account
cards.summary: Game settings are stored per signed-in account, with a remote profile row for sync. Delivered at source level per the storage doc.

cards.title: Skip the Mazer OAuth consent screen (Continue to Mazer?): live, needs a device check
cards.summary: Owner decision 2026-11-11: skip the Continue to Mazer? consent card. FawxzzyWeb PR #118 is MERGED (db5199e9) and the FawxzzyWeb release carrying it was aliased live on 2026-11-11. It auto-approves only for the exact Mazer client id, the exact Mazer redirect, the single basic scope, the name Mazer and a matching session user; Mazer already refuses callbacks without its own stored state and PKCE record. A production end-to-end sign-in in an emulated Galaxy S21 with the standing test account worked in headless Chromium. Still needs the owner's real-device sign-in check; kept in review until then. The auth screen anatomy doc rows (G6 and the consent bullet) are updated in the same change.

cards.title: Give accounts made on the account site a Mazer profile
cards.summary: Accounts made on the account site, which is what the Mazer Create Account button uses, got no Mazer profile row: only the in-Mazer sign-up path fired the trigger. The profile insert therefore failed with a not-null error on every sign-in, the leaderboard showed Choose a username with no way out, and settings never synced. 111 of 129 accounts had no profile and 9 of them had signed in to Mazer. A profile-ensure database function was applied to the live project on 2026-11-11 with the owner's explicit approval (one new function, no existing object changed; tested with the standing test account: it creates a generated Mazer-###### handle, is idempotent, and refuses a wrong user id and anonymous callers; profile rows 18 to 19). Mazer PRs 446 and 447 make the client call it once per bootstrap and on the settings write path instead of the failing insert; a username save ensures the profile first and a failed save shows a plain toast. Merged and deployed at main 8f757c76 (live bundle checked: the ensure call is present, the old direct insert is gone). The 9 affected players recover on their next load. Headless Chromium and mocks only: no real brand-new-account run and nothing checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Widen the sign-in window to 15 minutes and name each sign-in failure
cards.summary: A family member on a Galaxy S21 could not sign in and every callback failure showed the same message. Mazer's pending sign-in record expired after 5 minutes while the account site allows 15. PR 444 adds seven plain failure messages by class (took too long, came back to a different screen, cancelled, connection, session, storage, generic) and PR 445 wires them and widens the pending window from 5 to 15 minutes; the record is claimed exactly once, so a longer window adds no replay surface. The internal failure code is recorded in diagnostics only, and a new pending-expired code splits took too long from came back to a different screen. Merged and deployed at main 8f757c76. Unit tests plus headless Chromium with failures injected into the live scene at 390 and 1280 widths; no real sign-in round trip with a failure and nothing checked on a real phone. The fix is NOT proven against the original report: her root cause is unconfirmed (see MAZER-ACCT-016).

cards.title: Make the Create Account result honest
cards.summary: The account site Create Account form showed the success-styled notice Your account request is complete. You can continue to your account when a session is available. whenever sign-up returned no session (already registered, a weak new login choice, rate limit, network, unknown) and also after a successful sign-up without a Mazer return context. A family member reported a session was not available, which matches it. FawxzzyWeb PR 121 is MERGED (main bcfc556d) with an honest neutral message instead of the false success text, and a real session now continues straight into the account. It is NOT live: the FawxzzyWeb release carrying it is not yet aliased to the live domains. Residual: with auto-confirm on, a successful sign-up returns a session and a duplicate does not, so whether an account already exists can still be inferred by whether the user ends up signed in; closing that means turning auto-confirm off (see MAZER-ACCT-010). Not checked on a device.

cards.title: Decide the Create Account non-enumeration trade-off: accepted, auto-confirm kept
cards.summary: Owner decision recorded 2026-11-12: accept the residual signal and keep auto-confirm. With auto-confirm on, a successful Create Account returns a session and a duplicate does not, so someone could infer whether an account exists from whether they end up signed in. Closing that fully would mean turning auto-confirm off, which adds a confirmation step for every new player; the rest of the form no longer discloses it and the owner judged that cost not worth paying. No code or setting changed: this card is completed as a decision and has no device surface. Writing the accepted residual into the account site docs is not done and has no card yet.

cards.title: Add a leaderboard username editor (Edit name): merged and deployed
cards.summary: Owner decision 2026-11-12: build it. PR #450 (merged b3adf9be, live at main f8c16c72; live bundle checked for the Edit name control): an Edit name control on the pinned You row and on the Choose a username gate opens an inline editor. Names are 2 to 15 letters, numbers, dot, underscore or hyphen; errors are in plain language; Esc, back or a tap outside cancels; a save goes through the existing hardened save path, which ensures the profile first. The dead account-username-editor code was removed. Fixtures and mocks only: no real new-account run, keyboard safety checked by layout tests only, nothing checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Retire dead Mazer sign-up code: PRs #485 and #486 (stacked) open for review
cards.summary: Only the sign-up branch remains. The username-editor half is DONE in PR #450: the editor was built and the dead account-username-editor code was removed. What is left is the unreachable sign-up mode of the Mazer auth form (Mazer sign-up is an OAuth hand-off to the account site); remove it together with its tests and copy. Update 2026-11-13: OPEN FOR REVIEW, NOT MERGED. PR #485 (head 97641156, Wave 5C) removes the unreachable in-app sign-up mode and its tests; stacked PR #486 (head ea75d622, Wave 3B) removes five copy rows nothing reads. No shown copy changes. CI was red only on the stale generated work report check (also red on main), not on these changes. No browser run; nothing on a real phone. Follow-ups: MAZER-ACCT-038 and MAZER-UI-023.

cards.title: Confirm where sign-in lands on the installed Android app
cards.summary: One candidate for the Galaxy S21 report is that sign-in completes in a different context than the one that started it: the installed app versus a Chrome tab, where the pending sign-in record (kept per tab) is missing and the player sees the different-screen message. This needs a real Android phone. The owner runs the three device steps on the card. Related: MAZER-ACCT-003, the full installed-app proof. Not started.

cards.title: Record a failure code on every sign-in boot failure: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PRs #453 and #454 are merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). Every boot and sign-in failure now records a stable code of the form oauth-failure followed by the code name in runtime diagnostics: the new codes session_quarantined, session_read_failed and portal_navigation_failed sit next to the existing callback codes. Player copy stays plain and never shows the code, so a code is only readable with the runtime diagnostics switch (MAZER-ACCT-031). Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone, and no test yet pins every emitted code to the class map (MAZER-PROG-017).

cards.title: Keep the sign-in failure message readable: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: Measured first, as planned: before the fix the failure toast stayed 5015 ms at boot and 17 ms after a Sign in tap, too short to read. PRs #453 and #454 (merged, live at Mazer main 476c4789, headless Chromium only) hold the failure line until the next sign-in attempt and keep the toast on screen at least 8000 ms. Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Collect the Galaxy S21 sign-in details from the owner family member
cards.summary: Owner relay. The root cause of the Galaxy S21 sign-in failure is not confirmed; candidates are the misleading Create Account notice hiding a failed sign-up, the 5-minute Mazer window against the account site's 15 minutes, the installed app versus a Chrome tab, the 15-minute username rate limit, and duplicate usernames. Five questions are open, see the ask. Not resolved until she answers; the owner relays her answers.

cards.title: Give account-site players the username they typed on the leaderboard: function v2
cards.summary: Root cause: players who typed a username on the account site were given a generated Mazer-###### leaderboard name and their typed name was ignored. Fix, applied 2026-11-12 with the owner's explicit approval: the database profile function was replaced (version 2, same signature and permissions) so it adopts a valid unclaimed typed username, else a generated one, and never renames an existing profile. A one-off backfill also changed 8 existing generated-name profiles to their typed names (the owner approved 8 rows; the old values are saved in a locked table). Tested live with the standing test account (returns the existing profile unchanged, idempotent, wrong id refused, signed-out refused) and on a local throwaway database (15 cases). Privacy note: the typed username is public on the leaderboard and the account-site sign-up screen does not say so (MAZER-ACCT-018). No real new-account run and nothing checked on a real phone; the phone check is on MAZER-ACCT-006.

cards.title: Tell sign-up users their username shows on the leaderboard: live, phone check open
cards.summary: FawxzzyWeb PR #124 is merged (e03c7db8) and DEPLOYED with PR #125: the live account site (production aliases moved to build fawxzzyweb-4eoth56bm) shows the line This username shows on the Mazer leaderboard. on the sign-up screen, and the duplicate-sign-up notice sits out of the button label; the sign-in Edge Function (version 11) is live too. Read back on the live sign-up screen in a headless browser, not on a real phone. The owner has not yet confirmed the copy. Kept in review: deployed, headless only, nothing checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Re-read the username after profile creation mid sign-in: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PR #455 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium and mocks only). During an in-session sign-in the username is now read once more after the profile bootstrap, so the Choose a username gate no longer stays until a reload. Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Fix the four account-site usernames longer than 15 characters
cards.summary: Four account-site usernames are longer than the 15-character limit because the stored metadata on the account site bypassed validation; those players fall back to generated Mazer names. Plan: close the bypass and decide how to shorten the four names. Any data change needs explicit approval from the owner first. Related: MAZER-ACCT-030 (a few usernames over the limit are never indexed for sign-in by username). Not started.

cards.title: Refresh the header name after a rename: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PR #455 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium and mocks only): the header name now follows a rename in the same session without a reload. Whether the stored sign-in name also updates, which decides what the header shows after a reload, is not confirmed (MAZER-ACCT-033). Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Offer Edit name to a named player with no rank: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PR #455 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium and mocks only). A named player with no leaderboard rank now sees a pinned You row with dashes and an Edit name control, and an empty board offers Edit name. Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Account-site sign-out no longer races to login: merged, not live until aliases move
cards.summary: Code-read only, not reproduced: on the account site the sign-out event handler in usePortalSession can send the player to the login page before the return to Mazer runs. Proposed fix: a signing-out flag that stops the event handler racing the return. Separate design question: signing out on the account site does not end the Mazer sign-in session. Update 2026-11-13: FawxzzyWeb PR #130 (merged as 15ee11a1) adds a signing-out flag so the sign-out event handler no longer races the return to Mazer. MERGED-NOT-DEPLOYED to the live site until the production aliases are moved to the new build. Checked in tests only, not on a real phone. The separate design question (signing out on the account site does not end the Mazer sign-in) remains open.

cards.title: Receipt typed columns now filled by a trigger and backfill; run-quality use still open
cards.summary: APPLIED in production by the owner approval of the exact files and verified by readback. A before-insert trigger on the completion receipts fills the typed columns (completion time, path length and the rest), and a batched backfill filled 24,437 existing receipts in 13 batches of 2,000. Readback: all 26,308 receipts have a path length and completion time above zero, the trigger is enabled, no long transactions. Old values are saved in a preimage table; rollback files exist, but a rollback would overwrite later real values on those rows. Limits: the values are asserted by the client and outliers exist (one completion time above 42 million ms), so any run-quality gating must validate them; the typed columns are metadata only today. Lesson recorded: SQL hash guards must be computed from the LIVE function body (the repository copy had LF line endings while the live body had CRLF, so a first version of a stale-name script would have aborted on production), and the production SQL runner role cannot drop or disable triggers on the auth users table (owned by the auth admin role), so rollbacks drop the function with CASCADE. Not a device surface; kept in review until run-quality use is decided.

cards.title: Stored display name is now server-owned after a rename: live, device check open
cards.summary: Owner ruled that the server owns the stored display name and keeps it equal to the username. Client: PR #462 is merged and deployed (main 0537aa61): settings sync no longer writes the profile display name (production grants had let signed-in players edit it). Database: the patch is APPLIED, so the rename function now also writes the display name equal to the new username (one added line; applied from file hash c71a0586, live function hash verified 1b1fae6c, access rules unchanged, a rolled-back acceptance rename passed). NOT backfilled by design: 51 of 132 profiles still differ from their username and 25 are empty; an optional backfill file exists and is recommended NOT to run because it overwrites intentional values (MAZER-ACCT-034). Old installed app copies may still overwrite the display name until they update. Device check pending: rename on the Leaderboard, change Move Speed, reload; the name must be unchanged everywhere. Kept in review: headless Chromium and mocks only, not on a real phone.

cards.title: Username sign-in lockout (v4) live and sign-in verified; v5 proposal open, not applied
cards.summary: Before this change, repeated wrong tries on a username could also block the real owner's correct sign-in for a while, so someone else could lock a player out of username sign-in. Wrong tries are now counted per username and per client, so in the common case the lockout blocks the person who is guessing, not the real owner. FawxzzyWeb PR #129 (merged as 137d8a51) and sign-in function version 12 are live, and the database change (four new functions) was applied on 2026-11-12 with the owner's approval of the exact SQL, then read back and matched to the repo. Checked beforehand in an isolated in-memory database (45 of 45 checks) and by an independent read-only review; the function items it raised were fixed before merge. Update 2026-11-13: the coordinator verified a live sign-in with both sign-in methods (by username and by the account’s other method) after version 12; the live per-client behavior is not separately verified. Known limits are tracked privately. Kept in review: deployed and checked by the coordinator’s live sign-in, but not on a real phone. PROPOSAL ONLY, NOT MERGED, SQL NOT APPLIED: FawxzzyWeb PR #133 (lockout v5) adds failures-only check and record functions keyed by username and client, with no forwarded-address header, on top of the live v4. Nothing of v5 is live.

cards.title: Resolve the duplicate-username collisions with the oldest account winning
cards.summary: A few accounts share two usernames, which the new duplicate-username guard does not change. Proposed resolution file 05: the oldest account keeps the name and the others lose the username key only. They keep sign-in with the account address and lose the greeting name in the menu. Not applied: the owner must flip the pair_extension_recorded flag, then the flipped file is hashed for approval.

cards.title: Verify the before-user-created auth hook is registered at the provider
cards.summary: UNKNOWN: whether the before-user-created hook that calls the new username guard is registered at the auth provider. It needs an owner dashboard read or a live probe. Checked 2026-11-12 on production: the hook function reads the Mazer profile table as the auth admin role, which has a column grant on username plus a row-level access policy, so the Mazer branch should work if the hook is registered (read from the grants, not proven by a live sign-up). Registration itself is still not confirmed. Not started.

cards.title: Taken username named on the account site: merged, not live; Fitness patch proposed as text
cards.summary: A taken username and a generic database error during sign-up or rename reach the player as unclear copy on the account site and on Fitness sign-up and rename. Plan: map both to plain messages. Open question for the owner: how much a message may disclose about whether a username exists. Update 2026-11-13: FawxzzyWeb PR #130 (merged as 15ee11a1) shows "That username is taken. Pick another one." inline on the account site; a duplicate-account notice and a generic database error still read as neutral text. MERGED-NOT-DEPLOYED until the production aliases are moved. Caveat: that message only appears if the before-user-created hook is registered at the provider, which is UNKNOWN (MAZER-ACCT-028). The Fitness side is not changed: a patch for the raw sign-up error text (the auth actions file of the Fitness app) is proposed as text only.

cards.title: Shorten or index the usernames over 15 characters for sign-in
cards.summary: A few usernames over the 15-character limit (MAZER-ACCT-020) are silently never indexed for sign-in by username, so that way of signing in cannot find them; sign-in with the account address still works. Plan: shorten them or index them, together with MAZER-ACCT-020. Any data change needs approval from the owner first.

cards.title: Show a failure code a player can read off a phone
cards.summary: Sign-in failure codes (MAZER-ACCT-014) are only visible with the runtime diagnostics switch, which a player cannot easily turn on from a phone. Plan: show a short code on a surface that carries nothing that identifies a person, so a player can read it out. The owner decides which surface.

cards.title: A long header name is ellipsized instead of hidden: merged and live, device check pending
cards.summary: The header identity label hides a name that does not fit instead of cutting it with an ellipsis, so a long name leaves the header blank. Plan: ellipsize the name. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #470: the header name is always shown and cut with an ellipsis; it is hidden only when not even one character plus the ellipsis fits. Layout tests cover narrow widths. Device check pending, see the verify steps.

cards.title: Header follows the saved profile name after a reload: PR #487 open for review
cards.summary: The header follows a rename in the same session (MAZER-ACCT-021). Not confirmed: whether the rename also updates the stored sign-in name, which decides what the header shows after a reload. Plan: rename, reload and read the header, then fix if it reverts. Update 2026-11-13: FINDING CONFIRMED live on production with the standing test account: after a rename and a reload the header reverted to the old sign-in name while the leaderboard showed the new one (the account was renamed back through the same screen; no account was created). Cause: the header reads the sign-in name, a rename updates only the profile name. PR #487 (head 058f842b, OPEN, NOT MERGED, not deployed) reads the saved profile name once after sign-in so the header matches the leaderboard after a reload. Checked in a headless browser with a mocked profile call only. Not changed: the sign-in name itself, which is a shared identity decision for the owner.

cards.title: Optionally backfill the stored display name for already renamed profiles
cards.summary: The display name fix (MAZER-ACCT-025) only affects new renames. 51 of 132 profiles still have a display name that differs from the username and 25 are empty. An optional backfill file exists. Recommendation: do NOT run it, because it overwrites values players may have chosen on purpose. Owner decision; planning only, nothing applied.

cards.title: Sign-in outage handling: never strand the player on a provider error page
cards.summary: Outage on 2026-11-12, about 20:35 to 21:11 UTC: the account provider was down (its status page listed Database Connection Errors; the project sign-in and data origin answered 503, then gateway errors 521 and 525) and the owner was left on a blank provider 503 page inside the installed app with no way back. The provider recovered about 21:11 UTC. No data was lost and nothing was caused by our changes: the last database change was more than two hours earlier and sign-in by both routes (account address and username) worked after it. Fix, merged AND deployed (PR #466 at bc912691 and PR #467 at c80d8ce9; production Mazer c80d8ce9): Sign in first asks the account service whether it is up (a 4 second probe of its public discovery document, no sign-in details sent, never stored by the browser, success cached 30 seconds, failures never cached). A 5xx, 4xx, timeout, offline state or a gateway page without the cross-origin header keeps Mazer on Welcome and shows the plain failure line Sign-in is unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes. with diagnostics code oauth-failure:provider_unreachable; a probe refused in both modes (an extension or content-policy block) falls through and navigates as before. Owner decision accepted: a network error where a follow-up still gets an answer is treated as provider down. Live checks: the bundle carries the new strings and a real sign-in by both routes (account address and username) after the deploy succeeded with no errors. Measured: the first Sign in tap costs 100 to 250 ms more (187 to 247 ms without the probe, 293 to 500 ms with it) and 0 ms inside the 30 second cache window (cache unit-tested only). Kept in review: checked in headless Chromium with mocked failure shapes and against the live service only. NOT verified: a real phone or the installed app, a real outage, browser offline mode, an actual extension block, and a slow-but-up provider (the 4 second limit would block it; the first live probe during recovery took 4.5 seconds upstream).

cards.title: Welcome warms the account-service check so Sign in is quick: live, device check open
cards.summary: MAZER-ACCT-036 added a 4 second pre-flight probe before Sign in leaves the app; measured, the first tap costs 100 to 250 ms more and taps inside the 30 second cache window cost nothing. Proposal: run the same probe quietly when Welcome appears so the cache is already warm at the first tap. Needs a change to the Welcome scene (MenuScene, Wave 5C, a hot file), must never show a failure line by itself, and must not turn a slow-but-up service into a blocked Sign in. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #470: the Welcome screen runs the 4 second provider probe quietly when it appears and reuses the 30 second success cache. A failed warm-up shows nothing; only a Sign in tap shows the failure line. Measured with a mocked 230 ms probe: the first tap cost fell from 100 to 250 ms to 10 to 40 ms. Not measured against a slow-but-up real service on a phone.

cards.summary: A research pass defined an original music language: restrained, weather-touched and ancient, with small modal motifs, and explicitly no lifted melodies from existing game scores. cards.summary: Implemented: a PLAY clear shows the caption 'Level N' (the new displayed level) over the board for 700 ms using the existing motion durations, fading out; under reduced motion it is static for 400 ms. cards.summary: Implemented: when a clear moves the player to a stronger rank (levels 6, 11, 17, 23 and 31 on a normal ladder) the caption reads 'Rank D' style in that rank's colour for 1100 ms in place of the level caption; reduced motion shows it static for 400 ms. cards.summary: Owner decision 2026-11-11: remove the Level/Rank display. There is no rank letter and no Level N caption anywhere; the rainbow level numeral is the only level cue. cards.summary: Implemented: Quit to Menu quits at once when no move was made; after a move the first press (tap, click or the Q key) relabels the row 'Tap again to quit' for 3 s and the second press quits, with no browser dialog or modal. cards.summary: Today quitting or reloading discards the attempt and the next Start rolls a new maze, which is a free re-roll for a stuck player. cards.summary: Owner decision 2026-11-11: the menu demo is an independent attract loop on the ai-runner track and climbs one level per completed maze; play is unchanged. cards.title: Handle orientation flips mid-run: merged and deployed
cards.summary: PR #426 (merged and deployed): a flip of the screen aspect auto-pauses and refits; Pause shows 'Rotate back to keep playing' only while flipped and the one-tile corridor is under 24 css px. cards.summary: PR #423 (merged and deployed): the outbox flushes on the online event, the player sees one offline-saved notice per outage and a synced notice afterwards. cards.summary: PR #422 (merged and deployed): a one-line value statement, a mini-maze mark and a Link copied confirmation on the install gate. Feedback after a dismissed install prompt was NOT built. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Decide when input unlocks during the level intro
cards.summary: After a goal, input is locked about 2.5 s while the player marker is visible from 0.5 s. Unlocking earlier would speed play but touches timer, progression pacing and AI scoring, so it needs a product call. The owner also complained twice that build and deconstruct felt too fast, so pacing is sensitive. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

cards.title: Auto-pause when the page is hidden and fix lifecycle timing
cards.summary: A flow audit found that leaving the page did not pause a live run and that hidden time counted as run time. PR #392 opens Pause on hidden, page-hide and blur, excludes hidden time from the run timer and holds the intro and outro, and unblocks keyboard resume from the goal hold. Merged and deployed; real-device backgrounding is not yet verified.

cards.title: AI and play marker glide at steady speed instead of per-step eased tweens
cards.summary: The AI and play marker used a separate eased tween per step, so speed pulsed along a straight run. PR #414 (merge e35e814e) replaces them with continuous steady-speed motion; the menu demo walker speed variation went from 0.69 to 0.12 in headless measurement. Merged and deployed to production (main a983f2de, Ready). Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone or an installed app.

cards.title: Make player speed constant and 8% slower: merged and deployed
cards.summary: Owner request 2026-11-12. PR #449 (merged 73f754c2, live at main f8c16c72; live bundle checked: speed formula v2 present, v1 gone). The step speed used to depend on the Move Speed setting plus a level bonus of up to +0.10 and a pace-score bonus of plus or minus 0.05; now only the setting matters (formula v2) and the step rate is multiplied by 0.92. At the default setting the repeat interval is 139 ms (was 128), about 7.2 steps per second (was 7.8). The touch-stick caps scale to 113, 157 and 157 ms. The menu AI walker is separate and unchanged. Deviation: the stick caps were scaled too, which the owner did not explicitly ask for (a one-line revert). Tested headless and by unit tests; how it feels on a phone was not checked.

cards.title: Smooth maze generation, reveal and menu-demo pacing
cards.summary: Players saw freezes and unsynced beams around goal reach. A series of PRs precomputed the next maze during a hold, synced the delivery beam to the build, fixed reveal order and corrected menu-demo state carry-over across mode switches, including PRs #298, #302, #307, #310, #315, #316 and #317. Merged to main.

cards.summary: Edge-wrap topology diagnostics, a contract and an architecture test exist on main. The board card is complete at source level; no deployed or device claim is made.

cards.title: Fade wrap corridors out between levels 100 and 140 and price them
cards.summary: Wrap corridors used to switch off at level 120 and make level 120 about 88 steps longer than level 119. PR #404 fades them out from level 100 to 140 and prices each wrap's saving the way loops are priced, so a wrap cannot make a level easier than its target. The largest smoothed single-level step in levels 100 to 150 dropped from 19.4 times the median step to 2.3 times. It is merged and deployed on 2026-11-10. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and no wrap level was checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Unreachable floor islands appear in about 6% of generated mazes
cards.summary: About 6 percent of generated mazes carry a small group of floor tiles that no path reaches, visible as orphan tiles. Measured identical before and after the no-stub rule (MAZER-GEN-006), so it is an older generator behaviour, not a regression. Plan: find where the islands are created, then either wall them up or connect them without changing the felt-difficulty number, and add a property test over many seeds. Not started.

cards.title: No one-tile dead-end stubs in generated mazes
cards.summary: Owner request, with a screenshot of a late maze full of one-tile nubs: stop generating single-tile side branches. Mazer PR #464 is merged (951ef3cf) and deployed to production (the build before it was main 0537aa61). Rule: every generated ladder maze (levels 2 and up) has no dead-end branch shorter than 2 cells; a stub is a dead end whose only neighbour is a junction, and the start and goal caps are exempt. One-cell nubs are lengthened by one cell where the wall has room, else walled up, and each edit is kept only if the felt-difficulty number is unchanged; the fringe (levels 199 to 268 before this change) now carves 2 to 3 cell stubs only. The constant MIN_DEAD_END_BRANCH_CELLS is 2; 3 was not validated. Census before: 1.6 to 3.9 stubs per maze in the middle of the ladder and 51 to 57 per maze at level 268 and up, with 49 to 60 of 60 mazes holding at least one; after: 0 on every band and both boards. AI runner solvability 340 of 340 (levels 1 to 999, both boards, ranks E and S). Headless browser counts: phone level 50 4 to 0, level 150 1 to 0, level 300 32 to 0; desktop level 50 8 to 0, level 150 1 to 0, level 300 51 to 0. CONTRACT CHANGE: the fringe capacity falls from 70 to 20 cells, so the strictly rising ladder now ends at level 218 (was 268) and levels 219 and up are the plateau class. Late mazes lose held-out difficulty (dead ends 81-86 to 31 and decision points 34-40 to 11-13 at the plateau) while the felt number is unchanged; hazards (MAZER-HAZ-002) are meant to supply difficulty past 218. Player impact: most ladder layouts change (157 of 197 phone levels 2 to 198 and 166 of 197 desktop; every level 199 to 300); level 1 is unchanged; progress, receipts and the leaderboard are keyed by level number and seed, not layouts. Only the golden ladder fixture was regenerated. Pull request #464 and its commit named this rule MAZER-GEN-004 before that id was found already used by the wrap-fade card; this card is its board entry. Checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone; the owner judgement on the shorter rising ladder is open. Owner informal feedback 2026-11-12 evening, NOT a formal device check: "no single tiles so far". The ladder-end judgement and the preview levels 150, 218 and 300 are still unchecked.

cards.title: Straighter ladder mazes: less pointless snaking, rising ladder extended: PR #484 open
cards.summary: Owner request: reduce the pointless snaking in generated mazes. Measured: pointless snaking (a long run of 10 or more cells with 4 or more tight corners) held 31 to 47 percent of the floor on levels 20 to 218 and above; PR #484 cuts it to 3 to 14 percent by lowering the route share of the felt tuner and making carved branches keep their heading. The strictly rising ladder would extend to level 288 (was 218). OPEN, NOT MERGED, NOT DEPLOYED; PR #484 (head 316acd0a) now also carries a density fill that spends the freed cells on short side branches and breaks long empty halls, so the floor is back within 2 to 6 percent of the old maze and the largest blank patch is at or under the old one on most bands; known issues stated in the PR: the fill reads as a comb in places and the largest blank patch is slightly worse at level 150. Zero one-tile stubs and the AI runner solves 340 of 340 at the first head. CI was red only on the stale generated work report check. Headless browser and tests only; nothing checked on a real phone. If it lands, the preview jump list (MAZER-QA-007) and the ladder length (MAZER-PROG-019) follow.

cards.summary: Merged (PR #437) and live on main 24e15cc1. The brand test folder was never run by CI, which hid a conflict between two pull requests; it now runs in the verify workflow. Tooling only, no device surface.

cards.title: Stabilise load-sensitive tests: PR #489 open for review
cards.summary: Some tests pass alone every time but fail under parallel load: the endpoint tile pixel test at tile 25.44 and device pixel ratio 3, and vitest worker task-update timeouts. Plan: find the load sensitivity and make them deterministic. Update 2026-11-13: OPEN FOR REVIEW, NOT MERGED. PR #489 (head 8fed98b4) is test-side only: a vitest config with a 60 second default timeout, named heavy tests raised, half the logical CPUs as workers (CI keeps one), a setup file that yields after slow tests, an async runtime-eval test, and a trail frame-cost test that asserts the work instead of wall-clock time. Measured on one machine: one run with no load went from 4 failed tests to 0, and three runs at once went from 16 to 20 failed to 0 failed with exit 0. The remaining wall-clock asserts did not fail in any run and were left alone (follow-up suggested). CI was red on the stale generated work report check.

cards.summary: Merged (PR #441) and live in production at main 24e15cc1: one motion scale module that binds the shipped values (duration ladder, loop periods, reduced-motion crossfades, easing), with no visible change and no value changed. Acceptance criterion 3, removing dead tuning and unused DOM motion code, is deliberately NOT done: it is carried by MAZER-MOTION-007. The scene still uses its own constants until MAZER-MOTION-006. cards.title: Animate overlays, controls and the Start and splash transitions

cards.title: Cut canvas redraw cost: trail gate merged and live; backdrop bake still open
cards.summary: Re-scoped on 2026-11-12 after measuring. PR #459 is merged (7d6312eb) AND deployed to production (main 34b428fd, later builds include it): the play trail is rebuilt only when it can differ, with a gap of max(33 ms, 2x the last rebuild) capped at 250 ms, and the shortest route is memoised. Finding: while standing still the trail was rebuilt in full on every redraw, its cost grows with route length and plateaus at level 268; in a phone-sized headless profile at level 300 and 1x scale a still frame fell from 93 ms to 39 ms (a headless proxy, not a phone). Frame cost while walking is unchanged (MAZER-PERF-004 targets it). Device check pending: open a level 300 preview (previewLevel 300), stand still 10 seconds (should be smooth), then walk continuously (may still stutter). Still open: bake the backdrop, raise the throttle floor, and attach a real-device frame trace. Kept in review: deployed, checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone. Owner informal feedback 2026-11-12 evening, NOT a formal device check: "no more lag I think". Still phone-unverified: no frame trace and no timed check.

cards.title: Throttle colour-only redraws under reduced motion: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PR #456 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). Under Reduce Motion the colour redraws of the trail and the bleed-dock glow now share one 45 ms schedule, about 20 a second, with a largest step of 8 of 255 on the core and 17 of 255 on the bloom, so no visible stepping is expected. The glow was the dominant redraw source. Kept in review: not looked at on a real phone.

cards.title: Cheaper trail while walking: draft PR #461 needs an owner decision, no pixel parity
cards.summary: DRAFT PR #461 (head 476e5cf2, CI not started, not merged) splits the trail into a cached older part and a rebuilt tail. It cuts walking frame cost about 1.3 to 2 times (headless proxy, not a phone). Pixel parity with a full rebuild is impossible, because the trail colour changes everywhere every tick: on long routes colour, sheen and breath would step every 250 ms to 1 s instead of moving smoothly. This changes how the game looks, so it needs an OWNER decision after a phone check. Options: A ship it as is; B cap the cache epochs at 500 ms; C keep the smooth colour and accept the lag; D staggered per-chunk recolour or an OffscreenCanvas worker (recommended as the follow-up). Blocked on the owner decision; nothing merged. Owner informal feedback 2026-11-12 evening, NOT a formal check: "no more lag I think". Draft PR #461 stays unmerged; recommended to close it, since the lag no longer shows.

cards.title: Cheaper long-trail bloom: measured in PR #488, change needs an owner pixel review
cards.summary: On a long route the trail bloom is a large share of the remaining redraw cost. Plan: find a cheaper way to draw the bloom that keeps the halo as bright as today. Update 2026-11-13: PR #488 (open, not merged) adds a measurement script and written findings only; no bloom pixels changed. A cheaper bloom conflicts with the draft trail change (PR #461) and needs an owner pixel review before any build.

cards.title: Cap the trail canvas backing resolution on 3x phones
cards.summary: On 3x phones the trail canvas backing store is very large, which raises the cost of every trail redraw. Plan: cap the backing resolution on 3x phones. This changes how sharp the trail looks, so the owner reviews the pixels before it ships. Not started.

cards.title: Wrap-dock glow redraw on the shared 33 ms schedule: PR #488 open for review
cards.summary: Under full motion on the wrap levels (levels 6 to 145) the wrap glow triggers a full-board redraw. Reduced motion already shares one 45 ms schedule (MAZER-PERF-003). Plan: throttle the full-motion redraw the same way without a visible step. Update 2026-11-13: OPEN FOR REVIEW, NOT MERGED, NOT DEPLOYED. PR #488 (head bea7b1ef) puts the wrap-dock glow on the trail shared colour-redraw schedule (33 ms at full motion; reduced motion unchanged at 45 ms), so it no longer redraws the whole dynamic board every frame. Measured in headless Chromium on a wrap level: dynamic-board redraws per second 60 to about 36 (phone size) and 60 to about 35 (desktop size). Flagged for an owner eye: the sheen band crossing the trail head now steps up to 20 of 255 instead of 11. Nothing on a real phone. CI was red on the stale generated work report check.

The ladder (PR #395, replacing the draft in PR #385) merged on 2026-11-06 and was reported deployed on 2026-11-09. cards.summary: The felt-difficulty ladder rises strictly through level 198 on a fixed board with no zoom or size lever. What stays open is the lever after level 388: sign the hazard contract (MAZER-HAZ-002, hazardBudgetLevels starts at 388) or, only if hazards are rejected, a bigger board past a level, which is the zoom lever the owner ruled out. The owner wants levels to keep getting harder forever, so this decision cannot be settled by generation alone.

cards.summary: On a 390 phone at level 99 the tile is about 6.5 px, so the player and goal are tiny whatever the tile style; the Chip bake also costs 58-69 ms on the largest boards. Needs a product call on minimum tile size or zoom, which the owner deferred. On 2026-11-10 the owner delegated judgement calls on open design and flow picks to the build agent; no decision is recorded yet.

Merged to main.

cards.title: Extend the ladder to level 268 with side stubs the explorer does not pay for
cards.summary: The owner saw that the menu maze for level 18000 looks like a level 30 maze. Every level from 198 was the same maze class because the ladder steers on one explorer number and the board is full at level 198. Shrinking the route to raise that number made the other walkers 40 to 57 percent easier, so it was rejected. The new pull request adds exactly one more cell of short side stubs per level (the explorer does not enter stubs of 3 cells or fewer), which keeps the explorer number fixed and strictly orders levels 199 to 268 by cell count. At level 268 against 198 the maze has 38 route junctions instead of 12, 87 dead ends instead of 27 and the random walk takes 3.6 times as many steps. Levels 1 to 198 are byte-identical and levels 268 and above are one class again; the hazard hand-off now starts at 268. This is an open pull request, not merged and not deployed. The numbers are modelled walker difficulty, not player-tested, and the stubs are visible at a glance to a person. Merged and deployed to the live game on 2026-11-10. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone.

cards.title: Mastery tier to level 388: mazes also hard to solve from the goal end
cards.summary: Final audit of the progression engine on the frozen boards, without hazards. Finding: the ladder number is an explorer walking from the start, but the board is fully visible, so the same explorer walking from the goal pays only 0.3 to 0.6 of it on every level (475 against 759 at level 198 on the phone board). PR #415 adds a mastery tier for levels 269 to 388: route forks also point toward the start, so the goal end is just as deceptive, with no extra floor and the forward number unchanged. The share of such mazes rises by 1/120 per level to all mazes at level 388, each held to at least 740 steps from the goal end (measured 430 to 475 before, about 760 after). Levels 1 to 268 are byte-identical; the plateau and the hazard hand-off move from 268 to 388. Merged (merge 0a69f679) and deployed to production (main a983f2de, Ready). Honest limits: the ceiling is level 388, the ramp is statistical and not ordered for any two seeds; generation costs about 1.5 times the plateau class and about one desktop mastery build in twenty passed the 400 ms target at a 4x CPU throttle; the phone random walk reads 24 percent easier; no human play-test. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone or an installed app. Past 388 nothing on this board gets harder without hazards (MAZER-HAZ-002) or a bigger board. Superseded in part by MAZER-PROG-015: the tier is removed in the ladder v2 pull request (open for review) and the plateau returns to level 268.

cards.title: Double lure on levels 2-268 and the mastery tier removed (ladder v2): merged and deployed
cards.summary: Owner decision given (apply the double lure to levels 2 to 268). Merged in PR #420 (baa1c503) and deployed in cb750c70 and every later build; production is main b640f1da. Every maze from level 2 has route forks that also point toward the start and is held to a reverse floor (975 permille of its forward target, 740 at the top, 400 for a maze with a wrap corridor); level 1 is unchanged. The mastery tier of levels 269 to 388 is removed (ladder v2), so the plateau and the hazard hand-off are back at level 268 and levels 269 and up are the level-268 class. Measured on 48 seeds per level and board (modelled walkers): the cost from the goal end rises from 120 to 219 at level 10, 124 to 374 at 30, 190 to 484 at 100 and 475 to 767 at 198 (phone), forward number unchanged. Costs on record: the ceiling is now 268 (the phone two-way reading at level 388 is about 14 percent lower than the old ramp); the wrap rule keeps its corridors on 94 to 97 percent of mazes at level 100 (100 percent before); fewer looped mazes land at level 100; the held-out random walk reads 4 to 34 percent easier at 10 of 12 sampled cells. All walkers are modelled, no human play-test. Headless-only, not device-checked. Nothing checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Every sign-in failure code is pinned to the class map by a test: merged and live, review
cards.summary: Sign-in failures now record codes in diagnostics (MAZER-ACCT-014), and MAZER-ACCT-036 added provider_unreachable (code oauth-failure:provider_unreachable) for a down account service. Nothing stops a new code being emitted without an entry in the failure class map. Plan: add a test that lists every emitted code, including provider_unreachable, and fails when one is missing from the class map. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #469 statically scans the sign-in paths for every emitted failure code, including provider_unreachable, and fails when one has no class map entry. It runs in the normal verify workflow. Sign-in itself was verified live after this deploy; this change is a test only.

cards.title: Test every database change on a faithful scratch Postgres 17 and pin the live hash
cards.summary: Process rule from the 2026-11-12 database work: every SQL proposal is tested on a faithful scratch Postgres 17 and reviewed independently before the owner approves it, and any hash guard pins the md5 of the LIVE function body, not the repository copy (the live body had CRLF line endings, the repository blob LF, and a first guard would have aborted on production). Tooling to build: a reusable scratch Postgres harness and a read-only preimage query pack, both documented in the repository docs. Also record that the production SQL runner role cannot drop or disable triggers on the auth users table, so rollbacks use DROP FUNCTION with CASCADE. Update 2026-11-13: work has started and a worker is running. Not merged, and no pull request yet at the time of this sync.
