cards.summary: The owner asked to redo the Guide in both menu Settings and in-game Settings so it reflects the new look. A data-driven Guide sheet with icons drawn by the same functions as the board landed with the shared Settings sheet (PR #383, PR #386), and a drift test pins its claims to live game constants. It is kept current by the standing guide-sync rule.

cards.title: Redo the Leaderboard as a Settings-style sheet
cards.summary: The owner asked for the leaderboard to be redone entirely while keeping its icon. A first redesign shipped with the header and pause integration (PR #376), and PR #396 rebuilt it as a Settings-style sheet with a Back to Menu row, a pinned You row and seven states. Real leaderboard data on a phone has not been checked, and whether the column is called Rank or Place is an open naming call.

cards.title: Remove the Board Zoom setting
cards.summary: Board Zoom was a difficulty and framing lever the owner wanted kept out of play until obstacles and enemies are right. PR #396 removed it from Settings together with the leaderboard redesign, and the stored zoom value is scrubbed. Camera zoom stays deferred.

cards.title: Redo the Pause menu and remove the profile icon from it
cards.summary: The owner asked to redo the whole pause menu while keeping its icon and to remove the profile icon from it. The pause card is now Resume, Settings (collapsed) and Quit to Menu, and the profile icon is gone from Pause and Options (PR #376). Quit has no confirmation yet.

cards.title: Show the username beside the profile icon and drop the bottom Welcome line
cards.summary: The owner asked to remove the Welcome line and username at the bottom and show the username at the top left beside the profile icon, with no text background and some padding from the screen edge. This shipped in PR #376, with header edge padding in PR #382 and a clean label in PR #384. A CI check for the 320px label had to be loosened, and the label has not been seen on a high-density phone.

cards.title: Ship the Welcome sign-in screen and bound the sign-in loading state
cards.summary: A Welcome screen with one sign-in action, Create Account and account-recovery links and the legal row replaced the confusing pre-login screen, and the in-game Signing you in text now appears only for a real stored session (PR #376, building on the install gate and boot splash in PR #372). Real signed-in end-to-end testing is still outstanding.

cards.title: Fix menu accessibility: 320px clipping, 44px hit zones, Start tap recovery
cards.summary: Menu accessibility fixes: no clipping at 320px width, 44px minimum hit zones in the header, Start tap recovery and header edge padding. Merged in PR #382. The in-play pause control and the Guide header were not re-measured afterwards.

cards.title: Define one type scale and a second display typeface
cards.summary: The audit found 7 font stacks, 11 text sizes, text that shrinks to 8 px at 320 wide, and label formats that change with width. Proposal: keep Space Grotesk for body, add one squared techno display face for short uppercase labels, and set a fixed scale with a floor of 12 px for body copy. Not started beyond the font file itself.

cards.title: Ship a self-hosted Space Grotesk and wait for it before Phaser text
cards.summary: The declared brand font never actually loaded, so every device drew its own system font. PR #379 bundles Space Grotesk with the app and holds Phaser text until the font is ready, and PR #397 makes the capture harness ignore a harmless warm-reload preload hint. Merged; not yet checked on a real device.

cards.title: Add tone, scrim and motion values to the shared theme
cards.summary: Added the missing theme values the audit named (message tone colors, on-accent text, overlay scrim, motion durations) with a sync test and an off-theme color meter, with zero visual change. This only supplies the values; moving screens onto them is a separate card.

cards.title: Off-theme colour ratchet landed: new stray colour literals now fail, no source edits
cards.summary: About 290 hard-coded color values exist in the game code and only 5 match the theme; there are 5 different near-black backgrounds, 3 greens for energy and 2 mints. The plan is to map each to a theme value or a named material extension and add a lint so new stray colors fail. Not started; large because the menu scene file is huge. Merged to main, no player-visible change, so there is nothing to deploy-check. PR #481 (merged as 98f867e7) added a ratchet that fails when new off-theme colour literals appear and pinned the near-black 02080f; no source files were edited, so the existing stray colours remain and are not migrated yet.

cards.title: Make the in-play pause control a 44px target: shipped, now pinned by a test
cards.summary: The 44 px pause floor already shipped earlier (f06007c3, TOUCH_PAUSE_MIN_SIZE = 44). PR #428 (merged and deployed) adds the regression test. Measured in headless Chromium: 49 by 49 at 390 wide and 44 by 44 at 320 wide. Glyph size unchanged. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Build one shared button kit
cards.summary: There are 10 distinct button looks across 5 surfaces and no shared primary, secondary or destructive convention; START is a bare wordmark with a full-screen hit area. Proposal: 5 variants plus a toggle row and an explicit START hit zone. Not started.

cards.title: Frame the game on desktop instead of stretching the phone layout
cards.summary: At 1280x720 the menu is the phone layout stretched: tiny wordmarks and a 1100 px horizontal corridor. Proposal: a centered column or a scaled UI. Low priority because the game is phone-first.

cards.title: Pin the empty, loading, error, offline and username-gate states of the leaderboard
cards.summary: The empty, loading, error, offline and username-gate states already shipped with the 2026-11-06 leaderboard redesign (each has an icon, heading, line and action). PR #429 (merged and deployed) pins them with tests that use fixtures only; no real Supabase data was used. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Draw a player message toast and fix stale guest copy: merged and deployed
cards.summary: PR #430 draws the player message queue as a toast stack (3 rows, all four tones) and PR #431 removes every promise of guest play (copy test added); both merged and deployed. Not done and moved to new cards: routing auth, sync, username and boot errors into the queue (owner decision needed: remote sync is deliberately silent; see MAZER-UI-021), and moving the offline-notice strings into the message module copy tables (MAZER-UI-022). Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: UI rework migration: wave status report landed, umbrella to split pending the owner
cards.summary: UI component and layout standards are on main as registries. The full migration is under separately owned wave governance and remains open. Merged to main, no player-visible change, so there is nothing to deploy-check. PR #482 (merged as d5a29cee) is a read-only wave status report: the contracts layer is done, the migration layer (wave 3 and later) is not started, the DOM primitives are unused in production, and the menu scene is 16.6 thousand lines. The card stays an umbrella; the owner decision is whether to split it into children (menu scene decomposition, Wave 6 proof surfaces, future-phaser retirement).

cards.title: Decide the six design-board picks: font, quit confirm, start style, icons, backdrop, HUD
cards.summary: Remaining graphics work (icon atlas, button kit, backdrop unification, play HUD) waits on picks for the display font, Quit-to-Menu confirmation, START style, icon construction, backdrop and play HUD. The owner first asked to walk through them one at a time, then on 2026-11-10 said to stop asking and make the judgement calls. No pick has been recorded yet.

cards.title: Route auth, sync, username and boot errors into the message toast
cards.summary: The toast from MAZER-UI-018 draws the message queue, but auth, sync, username and boot errors are still not routed into it. Owner decision needed first: remote sync is deliberately silent, so showing sync failures changes that stance. Update 2026-11-13: not built. The decision is narrowed to a recommendation for the owner: keep sync silent, show boot errors on the splash, and toast only the service-worker warning that the offline cache could not update. Still planning until the owner decides.

cards.title: Move the offline-notice strings into the message module copy tables
cards.summary: Merged (PR #436) and live in production at main 24e15cc1. The offline-saved and synced notices now live in the message module copy tables; the strings, ids and tone are unchanged and the inventory test keeps the rows unique. Verified by unit tests and bundle contents only; no browser capture was recorded for it and it was not checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Narrow the menu diagnostics form mode to login only (wave 1C)
cards.summary: Follow-up to MAZER-ACCT-012. Once the in-app sign-up mode is gone (PR #485 and #486, open), the menu diagnostics form mode can only be login. Plan: narrow its type to login only. This is a wave 1C file and must not be mixed with other waves in one change. Not started.

cards.title: Ship the Chip board tile style as the default
cards.summary: The owner picked the Chip style for board tiles. The tile bake was added in the second integration and the Chip tiles, markers, wordmarks and Guide icons were wired in PR #387, with the Trace style kept as an alternate switch. Merged to main.

cards.title: Polish the Chip board: junction dots, player shape, start tile and goal alignment
cards.summary: The owner asked to remove the dots at path splits, make the player a rounded square that matches the chip tile shape, line the goal tile up exactly with its tile edges at every pixel ratio, and redesign the start tile in the same chip language. PR #402 makes all four changes and is merged and deployed to mazer.fawxzzy.com on 2026-11-10; it has not been checked on a real phone. The pad and ring on the end tiles were later removed at the owner's request (MAZER-VIS-013).

cards.title: Make the player trail iridescent with a gentle pulse
cards.summary: The owner wants the trail to look like a midnight-sun shimmer that shifts colour along its length and over time, with a gentle pulse. PR #402 adds a back-and-forth sweep through cyan, violet, orchid and apricot that avoids the player's green, the goal's red and the start's gold, clears the contrast floor against the dark underlay, and freezes to a static gradient under reduced motion. It is merged and deployed on 2026-11-10 and not yet checked on a real phone. The sweep was later made faster and a travelling sheen band added because the shift was too subtle (MAZER-VIS-013).

cards.title: Replace the edge diamonds with one new set that fires beams to and from all eight
cards.summary: The owner asked for one diamond set everywhere: sitting behind the title and menu UI, evenly spread along the screen edge with the bottom row flush to it, mirror-symmetric, and with lasers from the player out to all eight diamonds and from all eight out to the maze. The old diamond art and its image files were retired (PR #374, PR #375) and the layout and beam timeline were corrected (PR #384). Checked on test frames and the capture harness; not yet checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Make the edge diamonds orbit the screen during build and deconstruct
cards.summary: The owner wanted the eight edge diamonds to travel around the screen edge while a maze generates or deconstructs, not just spin in place. PR #388 adds one lap clockwise on build and one counter-clockwise on deconstruct, with the ring parked until the beams land. Merged and deployed; not yet checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Remove the leftover tile after deconstruct and the red square on the AI player
cards.summary: After a maze deconstructed a single tile could remain, and a red square followed the AI player when it moved. The deconstruct now switches the docks atomically (all at once or not at all) and the red marker was removed (PR #374). The lifecycle capture and analyzer found four causes of the leftover tile; two partial-strip findings are still unconfirmed.

cards.title: Restore the slower tile-by-tile maze build and deconstruct pacing
cards.summary: A timeline change made maze build and deconstruct almost instant, and the owner asked twice for the earlier pace back. PR #384 restored per-tile pacing: roughly two seconds to build level 1 and three to build level 20, with deconstruct somewhat faster than before. Whether it reads as smooth is the owner's call on a phone.

cards.title: Fix the missing maze deconstruction and fire the spawn beams after the build
cards.summary: The owner reported that the maze did not dissolve after reaching the goal and that the spawn beams fired before generation finished. Root cause was the Chip floor reveal mask treating an empty row limit as show-everything, so the full floor stayed drawn. Fixed in PR #393 with one shared reveal check; the intro now builds first, then the 8 beams fire, then the player appears. Merged and deployed; proven in a headless browser with a real key press, not yet on a real device.

cards.title: Add a goal beacon, minimum-size goal marker and legible trail on dense boards
cards.summary: On small Chip tiles the goal and trail were hard to read. PR #394 adds a goal beacon, a minimum-size goal marker and a more legible trail. Earlier goal-star work landed in PRs #321, #330 and #331. Merged to main.

cards.title: Make the player easy to find and fix readability checkpoints
cards.summary: The player was hard to find on dense boards and four palette readability checks failed on the Chip tiles with nothing asserting them. PR #399 adds a locator ring and soft glow in the player's own green with a find-me pulse on spawn, unpause and idle, and raises the model floor luminance so all 20 readability checkpoints pass. Real-phone cost and feel are not measured.

cards.title: Regenerate the HUD icons as one matched set and atlas
cards.summary: The three header icons are 1254 px AI-style PNGs in three different styles and glow treatments, shown at under 25 px, 1.5 MB in total. Plan: redraw as one outline icon family from scripted SVG, bake a single small atlas, and add the missing glyphs (close, check, info, share, install). Not started.

cards.title: Unify the backdrop across boot, install gate and sign-in
cards.summary: Three visual dialects exist: the game (black space, dot matrix), the teal-black install and sign-in pages, and the account portal. Plan: one near-black canvas color, calmer starfield on gates, the app icon on the install screen, and a dot-matrix wordmark on boot. Portal alignment is in a separate repo. Not started.

cards.title: End markers without a box, start arrow, visible trail shift, matched diamonds
cards.summary: After PR #402 went live the owner asked for five changes. (1) The square pad behind the goal star and start marker is gone: the star and play arrow sit directly on the board tile with a thin dark outline for legibility. (2) The start arrow points the way the player will first move (the first step of the solution path; down on the portrait level 1, right on landscape). (3) The trail colour shift is now clearly visible: a shorter, faster hue sweep plus a travelling white sheen band that also shifts the hue, still at least 3:1 against the chip tile and static under reduced motion. (4) The edge diamond border is always the live trail colour and (5) the colour inside the diamonds and the beams is always the player's green, both from one shared palette module. The Guide copy and icons were updated. Open as a pull request; not merged, not deployed, not checked on a real phone. Merged and deployed to the live game on 2026-11-10. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone.

cards.title: Remove backdrop stars, centre the end markers, lighten the long trail draw
cards.summary: After the previous polish went live the owner reported still stars behind the maze, a trail whose colour does not visibly move, and an end star and start arrow that are off centre and reach the tile edge. Merged (pull request 411) and deployed to the live game on 2026-11-10. The coloured four-point stars are gone and no star is drawn while the background is not animating. The star and the arrow are now centred as a whole (outline included) and sit inside the lit rim at every tile size and pixel ratio, with new pixel tests. The trail glow is drawn on a downscaled scratch canvas, which lightens the long-trail draw. The corner flake was traced to unseeded random sparkles. Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone: a touch-drag capture on the live game shows the trail colour changing frame to frame. The owner report that the trail looked static on his phone is not reproduced, and the real cause there is not proven. The trail is still when Trail Shine is Off or the device asks for reduced motion.

cards.title: Fix image and vector misalignment: whole-pixel placement and camera origin
cards.summary: Reported: the end star sat off centre and the trail and player glow jumped as they moved. Root cause: Phaser rounds image positions to whole pixels but not vector graphics, plus a half-pixel camera offset on odd-width viewports; the end star was 2 device pixels off centre at 2.625 and 2.75 pixel ratios and the trail and player glow jumped a CSS pixel as they moved. PR #416 (merge a983f2de) places images on whole pixels, sets the camera origin to 0,0 and snaps the bake margins and maze origin to whole pixels. Merged and deployed to production (Ready, live bundle verified to contain the new code). Checked only in headless Chromium at several viewport sizes and pixel ratios, not on a real phone or an installed app.

cards.title: Dock pulse takes trail head colour; backdrop stars restored, shards and runes off
cards.summary: Visual cleanup in PR #416 (merge a983f2de). The bleed-off dock pulse now uses the trail head colour (the same function as the edge diamonds) and is centred on the cell. Backdrop stars are restored: every star is drawn as a round point of light with a deterministic start layout and no tails. Backdrop shards, drift runes and corner sigils are no longer drawn (the drawing code is still in the source, see MAZER-VIS-017). Merged and deployed to production (Ready). Checked only in headless Chromium, not on a real phone or an installed app.

cards.title: Purge the disabled backdrop glyph drawing code and its pinned source-string tests
cards.summary: Merged (PR #439) and live in production at main 24e15cc1. The shard, rune and sigil drawing code and the two disabled-glyph flags are removed; a behaviour test replaces the source-string pins and the star pixel baselines are unchanged. The unused pure generators in the backdrop module remain on purpose (that file belongs to a different wave than the scene file) and are carried by MAZER-VIS-027. Checked by unit tests and pixel baselines only, not on a real phone.

cards.title: Trail colour reported static on the owner phone: not reproduced, needs device data
cards.summary: The owner reports the trail colour looks static on the phone. Headless runs do not reproduce it: the colour at a fixed point changes strongly every 250 ms. Not fixed and not confirmed as a defect. Needs the phone model plus the Trail Shine and Reduce Motion settings from the owner, or a real-device check. Not started. Update 2026-11-11: the menu demo colour clock was play-only and is fixed (PR #421, deployed), so on a phone the remaining likely cause is the OS Reduce Motion setting or Trail Shine off; this still needs the owner phone settings. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Remove the Level N and Rank X captions
cards.summary: Owner feedback: the white Level N caption above the rainbow level numeral and the rank display should go. PR #419 deletes the level-complete and rank-up captions; the rainbow level numeral is now the only level cue and no rank letter is shown anywhere. Merged and deployed. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Fix the trail corner-cut when stepping back over the trail
cards.summary: Owner feedback: the player trail broke and twitched when walking backwards along it. A step back dropped the arrival tile from the drawn path, so the line cut every corner and snapped when the glide ended. PR #419 (resolveTrailGridPathWithHead) keeps the arrival tile on a backward step. Headless Chromium, level 12 preview, 20 steps out and 20 back: 9 per-frame head jumps before, 0 after. Merged and deployed. Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: Run the trail colour clock on the menu demo too
cards.summary: Owner feedback: the trail colour was not shifting like the rest of the game. The trail animation clock only ran in play, so on the menu demo its colour varied with distance, never with time. PR #421 runs the clock on the menu under the same conditions as play (not reduced motion, Trail Shine on, board settled, no overlay). Merged and deployed. Headless Chromium: the clock advanced over 3 s and the colour changed. The owner phone may still look static from the OS Reduce Motion setting or Trail Shine off (see MAZER-VIS-018). Headless-only, not device-checked.

cards.title: AI player and play player share one marker drawn like the end tiles
cards.summary: Merged (PR #442) and live in production at main 24e15cc1. One shared marker module now draws the marker for play, the menu demo AI and the Guide icon: same block size, keyline, glow and device-snapped centre as the end tiles. The ring is now tile-sized and inside the player tile; the old crosshair ticks, the halo and the flat-square AI marker are removed. The find-me ping stays play-only. Frame cost is about +0.07 ms per call in headless Chromium. Checked only in headless Chromium and unit tests, not on a real phone; the menu AI marker check is on the phone checklist (MAZER-QA-001).

cards.title: Round the player ring to the cap-tile shape on start and goal: deployed, check pending
cards.summary: PR #458 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). On the start and goal tiles the player ring now follows the rounded cap-tile corners instead of poking past the dead-end disc. The ring still switches shape abruptly halfway (MAZER-VIS-028). Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Make the marker diagnostics report the real block size: deployed
cards.summary: PR #458 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). The marker style diagnostics now report the real drawn radii, 0.3 and 0.5 of a tile, instead of the old ratios 0.46 and 0.72. This is a diagnostics-only change with no player-visible surface, so no phone check is needed beyond MAZER-VIS-023.

cards.title: Snap the trail head to the marker device pixel: deployed, device check pending
cards.summary: PR #458 is merged and live at Mazer main 476c4789 (live bundle strings checked, headless Chromium only). The trail head is now snapped to the same device-pixel centre as the player marker. Four trail corner raster baselines were regenerated on purpose. The head does not yet follow the wall-bump nudge of the marker (MAZER-VIS-029). Kept in review: nothing is checked on a real phone.

cards.title: Decide dense-board player prominence after the tile-sized ring
cards.summary: At 8 px tiles the old ring was 22 px across; the ring is now tile-sized, so on dense boards it is a thin ring that shows only from 2x displays, and the find-me ping in CSS pixels is what finds the player. Owner recommendation: accept this. Alternative: a screen-pixel floor applied to the glow only. Needs the owner; no decision recorded.

cards.title: Unused backdrop shard, glass shard and rune generators deleted: merged and live
cards.summary: Follow-up to MAZER-VIS-017. The pure shard, rune and sigil generators in the backdrop module are unused but remain because that file belongs to a different wave than the scene file. Plan: delete them in their own pull request, together with the pinned source assertions and the shard-count tests. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #477 deleted the unused backdrop shard, glass shard and rune generators with their pinned source assertions and shard-count tests. Star backdrop behaviour and raster baselines are unchanged.

cards.title: The player ring morphs between cap and chip shape, no pop: live, device check pending
cards.summary: The player ring now follows the cap-tile shape on start and goal tiles (MAZER-VIS-023) but switches between the cap and chip shape abruptly at the halfway point when the player enters or leaves such a tile. Plan: blend the ring between the two shapes. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #478: the ring blends between the cap and chip shape across the start and goal tile instead of switching at the halfway point; reduced motion collapses the morph.

cards.title: The trail head follows the marker wall-bump nudge: merged and live, device check pending
cards.summary: A blocked move nudges the player marker about 2 px (MAZER-MOTION-003), but the trail head, now snapped to the resting centre of the marker (MAZER-VIS-025), does not follow the nudge. Plan: apply the same nudge to the trail head. Merged and deployed on main 62f36472 (production build fawxzzy-mazer-4djzxfozs, previous build fawxzzy-mazer-ldk3ncpod), checked only in headless Chromium and tests, not on a real phone. PR #478: the trail head follows the marker wall-bump nudge through a head-only offset; reduced motion collapses it. Known quirk: a bump perpendicular to the last trail segment skews that segment by up to 2 px for about 110 ms.

cards.title: Redesign the diamond lasers and fill and drain the diamond with the beam
cards.summary: Owner request 2026-11-13: redesign the diamond lasers and make the beam fill and drain the diamond. This is teleport presentation work in wave 4D-B. Work has started and a worker is running; no pull request yet, nothing built, nothing merged.
